providers.title: Providers
providers.description: Set up providers once, then pick any of their models in a chat.
providers.emptyDescription: Add a cloud provider with an API key, or run Ollama, llama.cpp or another local AI server on this server to run models locally.
providers.removeDescription: Its key is deleted from this server. Chats that used its models stay, and ask for another model.

defaults.title: Defaults
defaults.description: New chats start with the default model. Each chat can switch model at any time.
defaults.limitInvalid: Enter an amount above 0, or leave it empty
defaults.defaultModelHelp: Only models that can use tools work with the assistant.
defaults.titleModelHelp: Optional. A small, cheap model is enough.
defaults.advisorHelp: Optional. A stronger model the assistant can ask for a second opinion, once per step. Its provider sees the question the assistant writes, not the whole chat, and what it costs counts toward the spend limit.
defaults.refineHelp: Before it finishes, the assistant reviews its answer and writes it again, fixed. At least one more model request per reply, so slower and costlier; the first draft stays folded in the reply.
defaults.spendLimitHelp: A chat stops once it has cost this much. Only applies to models with known prices; local models are free.

shell.title: Shell
shell.description: Let the assistant ask to run commands on this server, as the user Athena runs as. You approve every command before it runs, and each one is written to the audit log.
shell.enabledHelp: Off by default. Athena's own tools (apps, packages, files) don't need it.
shell.allowedHelp: One per line. Every program in a command is checked, including each part of a pipe (<pipe/>) or chain (<and/>, <semi/>); others are refused before you're asked. This guards against mistakes, not a determined model: an allowed program can start others, so read each command before you approve it. Empty means no shell.
shell.badNameHelp: List programs only, one per line, without shell operators like ; | & > or $.

tools.title: Memory and research
tools.description: What the assistant can keep between chats and look up on its own.
tools.memoryHelp: Keeps notes that later chats read, such as how this server is set up. Each admin has their own. Turning it off keeps the notes; the assistant just stops using them. Notes that look like hidden instructions are refused and written to the audit log.
tools.webHelp: Searches the web with Exa and reads the pages it finds. The server needs an EXA_API_KEY environment variable before any search works.
tools.skills: Skills are instructions the assistant loads when a task needs them. Add one as a folder with a SKILL.md file in assistant/skills inside Athena's data folder.

advanced.dockerHelp: Runs commands and edits files in an isolated container instead of on this server. Pulls a small Python image on first use.
advanced.codingHelp: Reads AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md from assistant/code-workspace in Athena's data folder, and reads or writes files there. Reading is free; every write shows an Approve/Deny card first.
advanced.durableHelp: Checkpoints each model request and tool call, so an interrupted chat resumes instead of repeating paid work. Needs pgtask and a Postgres database (ATHENA_DURABLE_EXECUTION_DATABASE_URL); without them it changes nothing. Experimental: a crash and resume hasn't been tested end to end yet.
advanced.browserHelp: Not available yet: it waits for a browser-use release that installs alongside the rest of the server. Turn it off.

review.title: Review tool calls
review.description: A second model checks each action before it reaches your Approve/Deny card and approves the clearly safe ones, so you only see the risky ones.
review.modelHelp: Its provider sees each call's name and arguments, not the whole chat. Every check is one more model call and counts toward the spend limit.
review.helpWithModel: Safe actions are approved for you; risky ones still reach your card.

integrations.title: Hosted integrations
integrations.description: MCP servers Athena runs for the assistant (GitHub, Linear, Notion, …). Each has an encrypted token, and its actions go through your Approve/Deny card.
integrations.removeDescription: Its token is deleted from this server. Chats that used its tools will no longer have them.

sections.modelsDescription: Where the assistant's models come from and which ones it uses.
sections.toolsDescription: What the assistant can do besides managing apps, packages and files.
sections.advancedDescription: Off by default. Each one needs something extra on the server.

adminOnly: Only admins can set up the assistant

providerDialog.description: Keys are stored encrypted on this server and never sent back to the browser.
providerDialog.name: Name
providerDialog.nameHelp: Shown in the model picker, e.g. “Work key”.

integrationDialog.description: The token is stored encrypted on this server and never sent back to the browser. Leave the token empty when editing to keep the stored value.
integrationDialog.commandHelp: The program that runs the MCP server, e.g. npx or uvx.
integrationDialog.argsHelp: Comma-separated arguments; no shell is used.
integrationDialog.tokenEnvHelp: The env var that receives the decrypted token on each turn.
integrationDialog.tokenHeaderHelp: The HTTP header that receives the decrypted token on each request.
integrationDialog.kindFixed: The kind can't be changed after creation; remove and re-add to pick another.
integrationDialog.name: Name
integrationDialog.nameHelp: Shown when the integration is listed.
integrationDialog.tokenPlaceholder: API token or OAuth access token
integrationDialog.tokenHelp: Left empty when editing, the stored token is kept unchanged.

setup.title: Set up the AI assistant
setup.description: Optional. The assistant answers questions about this server and, with your approval, installs apps and manages packages and files.
setup.addHint: Add a cloud provider with an API key, or a local one such as Ollama, LM Studio or llama.cpp.
setup.defaultModelHelp: New chats start with it. Only models that can use tools work with the assistant.
setup.later: You can change this later in Settings → AI.
